result.title: TurboWAM: Learning What Matters for Fast World Action Models
result.summary: World action models have demonstrated promising performance in robot policy learning, yet their high inference latency remains a critical bottleneck for real-world deployment. Recent approaches have sought to improve inference efficiency by reducing test-time future-frame imagination or accelerating action prediction. However, these methods often leverage representations from all video world model layers without explicitly considering their varying relevance to action prediction, leading to redundant computation and suboptimal representation utilization. In this work, we propose TurboWAM, a fast world action model that efficiently aggregates structured world representations conditioned on action predictions. Specifically, TurboWAM introduces a structured world representation aggregation module that adaptively fuses representations from different world model layers according to their relevance to the evolving action denoising state. Furthermore, TurboWAM employs a structured action supervision mechanism that adaptively modulates gradients from action supervision across different world model layers during backward propagation, facilitating world representation learning. During inference, by reducing the number of world model layers executed and caching relevant representations across action denoising steps, TurboWAM substantially reduces computational overhead. Extensive experiments on multiple robot manipulation benchmarks demonstrate that TurboWAM achieves low inference latency while maintaining competitive task success rates compared with state-of-the-art methods.

AI.brief_summary: TurboWAM 针对 world action model 推理延迟高的问题，提出按动作去噪状态自适应融合不同世界模型层的表示，并在反向传播中调制各层动作监督梯度，推理时通过减少执行层数、缓存相关表示来降低计算开销。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按任务相关性选择层表示、跨去噪步缓存内部状态的做法，可能为 LVR 中「哪些深度的视觉状态真正被下游使用」以及缓存与层深度对 latent 相似度的影响提供可供核查的线索。
